transcript.text: Shark NZ801UK anti hair wrap upright - suction has gone really weak over the last couple of weeks, barely picks up crumbs. Have emptied the bin. Any ideas before I buy a new one?

Yes — this is very often fixable without replacing the vacuum. A gradual loss of suction after the bin has been emptied is most commonly clogged filters, then a blockage in the airflow path. 1. Unplug it. Remove the filters and inspect them. If they are grey, dusty or matted, wash the washable filters in cold water only; do not refit them until completely air-dry, ideally 24 hours or longer. A filter that is even slightly damp can itself cause poor suction. 2. While they are out, check the hose, wand, floorhead neck and the bin inlet for a plug of fluff or debris. Look through the detached hose/wand rather than poking tools into them. 3. Turn the floorhead over and remove hair or thread wrapped around the roller; it should turn freely by hand. If suction is still weak with clean, fully dry filters and no blockage, the next possibilities are a split hose, a bin/seal not seating properly, or a restriction in the cyclone. Check the filters first before spending money on parts or a replacement.
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]

Found the filters under the bin. Never washed them, didn't know they were there. Foam one is grey, the felt one is caked with fine dust. Hose and wand are clear, roller just has a bit of fluff and spins freely. No burning smell. Shall I wash both filters then?

Yes — wash both the foam and felt filters. Their condition is the strongest explanation for the gradual loss of suction. 1. Switch off and unplug the vacuum. Rinse both filters thoroughly in cold water only, gently squeezing and flushing out the dust. Do not use detergent, hot water or a radiator/hairdryer.
2. Leave them somewhere warm and airy until completely dry — allow at least 24 hours, longer if either still feels cool or damp inside. Do not run the vacuum without the filters or refit them damp.
3. While they dry, remove the small fluff from the roller and check the bin and lid are properly seated when you reassemble it. Once dry, refit them and try it on a hard floor. If suction is still weak, the next likely causes are a dust blockage in the cyclone/bin inlet or a bin seal not seating properly; that would be the point to inspect those areas rather than buy a new vacuum.
ok, will wash them both and leave them 24 hours. Will report back once they're dry.

Once they have dried fully and are refitted, test the vacuum on a hard floor and let me know whether suction is normal again or still weak. If it is still weak, the next most likely areas are a fine-dust restriction in the cyclone/bin inlet or a bin lid/seal allowing an air leak. At that point, inspect the bin inlet and cyclone openings with the vacuum unplugged, and check the bin and lid sit flush with no damaged or displaced seal.
Washed both and left them 24 hours until fully dry. Refitted and tried it on the hard floor - massive difference, suction is back to like new. Thanks.
That suggests it: the clogged filters were restricting the airflow, not a failed motor or anything needing replacement. No need to buy a new vacuum. Is there anything else you’d like help with?
